title: Beyond Shares: Understanding Futures and Options in Our Market
description: Futures and Options (F&O) are financial contracts whose value comes from another asset, like a share or a stock index. They let you agree to buy or sell somet.

faq.a: An underlying asset is the financial instrument (like a stock, index, or commodity) from which a derivative contract's value is derived. You don't directly trade the underlying asset in F&O, but its price dictates the value of your contract.

Expiry refers to the date on which a derivative contract ceases to exist. On this date, the contract is settled based on the underlying asset's price, and positions are closed. For many NSE contracts, monthly expiry falls on the last Tuesday of the month, or the preceding trading day if it's a holiday.
Margin is a security deposit you need to keep with your broker to trade F&O contracts. It's a fraction of the total value of the contract and acts as a buffer against potential losses.

Yes, any individual with a trading account can trade F&O. However, due to the complexity and high risk involved, it's crucial to understand how they work and the potential for significant losses before participating.

faq.q: What is the minimum investment for F&O?
faq.a: There isn't a fixed "minimum investment" like buying one share. F&O contracts are traded in "lot sizes" (a fixed number of underlying units). The actual capital required depends on the lot size, the contract value, and the margin set by the exchange and your broker.
